title: Precision Astigmatism Management: LRIs vs. Arcuate Keratotomy
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to corneal relaxing incisions for the correction of astigmatism. This poster contrasts the biomechanics, techniques, and outcomes of Limbal Relaxing Incisions (LRI) and traditional Arcuate Keratotomy (AK) for ophthalmologists and surgical fellows.

branches: LRIs: Incisions at the peripheral limbus (90% depth)
AK: Incisions within the clear cornea (more central)
Goal: Flatten the steep meridian and steepen the flat meridian

sections.title: LRI vs. AK: The Core Comparison

rows: Inside the clear cornea (7-8mm optical zone)
Slower; risk of foreign body sensation

sections.title: Biomechanics: The Coupling Rule
sections.content: The 'Coupling Ratio' in incisional surgery is ideally 1.0. This means for every 1.0 Diopter of flattening in the incised meridian (steep axis), there is an equal 1.0 Diopter of steepening 90 degrees away (flat axis). Consequently, the Spherical Equivalent (SE) remains unchanged. If the coupling ratio is >1, the SE moves toward hyperopia; if <1, it moves toward myopia.

sections.title: Etiology & Indications
content: Pre-existing corneal astigmatism in cataract patients
Residual astigmatism after Toric IOL placement
Post-penetrating keratoplasty (PKP) astigmatism (primarily AK)
Patients desiring spectacle independence but ineligible for Laser Vision Correction (LVC)
Low to moderate astigmatism (0.75D to 2.50D)

sections.title: Red Flags: Absolute Contraindications
content: Keratoconus or Forme Fruste Keratoconus (FFKC)
Pellucid Marginal Degeneration (PMD)
Significant Corneal Thinning or Ectatic Disorders
Prior Radial Keratotomy (RK) - Risk of 'Starfish' wound dehiscence
Active Ocular Surface Disease or Severe Dry Eye Syndrome
Active Infectious Keratitis
Connective Tissue Diseases (Rheumatoid Arthritis, SLE) due to risk of melt

sections.title: Pre-operative Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Manifest Refraction (Verify cylinder axis and power)
Step 2: Corneal Topography/Tomography (Rule out ectasia; identify steep axis)
Step 3: Manual Keratometry (To confirm steep axis regularity)
Step 4: Ultrasonic Pachymetry (Measure thickness at the intended incision site)
Step 5: Apply Nomogram (e.g., Donnenfeld or Nichamin) to calculate arc length

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Manual Diamond Knife
content: Step 1: Reference Marking (Mark 0-180 axis while patient is upright to avoid cyclotorsion)
Step 2: Intra-operative Marking (Mark the steep axis and the arc length degrees)
Step 3: Knife Depth Setting (Set diamond blade to 600μm or 90% of thinnest pachymetry)
Step 4: Fixation (Stabilize globe with Fine-Thornton ring)
Step 5: Incision (Steady, perpendicular stroke along the marked arc)

content.explanation: Steep Axis: Always incise the STEEP meridian. Arc Length: Longer arc = more correction. Location: Limbal (LRI) or Arcuate (AK). Thinnest: Check pachymetry before cutting.

sections.title: Femtosecond Laser Arcuate Keratotomy (FLAK)
content: Precision: Micron-level accuracy in depth (typically 80-90%)
Geometry: Ability to create truly vertical or angled side-cuts
Intrastromal AK: Incisions that do not break Bowman's or Epithelium (reduces infection risk)
Repeatability: Lower surgeon variability compared to manual diamond knives
Integration: Often performed as part of Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Cataract Surgery (FLACS)

sections.title: Instrumentation Checklist
content: Mendez Degree Gauge (for 360° orientation)
Fine-Thornton Swivel Fixation Ring
Preset Diamond Knife (600 micron standard for LRI)
Calibrated Micrometer Diamond Knife (for AK)
Gentian Violet or Sinskey hook for marking

rows: Wait for healing; suture if persistent

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always measure pachymetry at the limbus; it is significantly thicker than the center.
For 'Against-the-rule' (ATR) astigmatism, remember that incisions are placed horizontally (3 and 9 o'clock).
If the patient is over 70, consider reducing the arc length by 10% due to increased corneal rigidity.
Intrastromal incisions (FLAK) provide less correction than penetrating incisions but have a superior safety profile.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
sections.content: Recent studies (e.g., by the American Academy of Ophthalmology Ophthalmic Technology Assessment Committee) suggest that while FLAK is more precise in depth than manual LRI, the visual outcomes at 6 months are often comparable. Modern nomograms now incorporate Posterior Corneal Astigmatism (PCA), which typically adds ~0.5D of 'Against-the-rule' astigmatism, necessitating a slight over-correction of 'With-the-rule' steepness.
